approach: Add a pid file (`<state root>/drain.pid`, next to `drain.stop`) that `athena drain` writes at start and removes on exit, holding pid, a process start marker, the build string and a timestamp. All lifecycle code goes in `crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs`. A `Procs` trait (`start_marker(pid)`) is the only way code asks whether a drain is alive. `RealProcs` reads /proc/<pid>/stat field 22 on Linux and runs `ps -o lstart=,stat= -p <pid>` elsewhere (lookup by pid, never by name); a zombie counts as gone. Nothing matches command text and nothing sends a signal; stop uses the existing stop file. New pieces: `drain_state()`, `PidGuard::acquire()`, `stop_and_wait()`, `restart()` over a `Lifecycle` trait, and `guarded()` (the stale check is an injected closure). Revision for round 1 findings: (1) `restart` no longer trusts its first rebuild. It rebuilds, then stops and waits for the old drain, then asks `Lifecycle::installed_stale()` whether the INSTALLED binary is behind HEAD (reads `<installed> --version`, not the running binary's build) and rebuilds again, now with nothing landing, before it spawns; a failed or still-stale rebuild spawns nothing and says so. (2) Waiting for the old drain has no limit by default and prints progress; on `--timeout` the error says the stop is still asked, no new drain will start, and what to run next. (3) When there is no pid file, `restart` says an older-build drain cannot be seen, writes no stop file (the new drain would delete it anyway) and spawns; README and CHANGELOG state this one-time transition. (4) `guarded` keeps `drain.stop` when the pid file already names this pid (the exec carry-over) and removes it only when the file was missing, dead or recycled. (5) Help and README say the restarted drain runs in the background in its own process group, not a new session, and logs to `<state>/drain.log`. Every new test lives in `#[cfg(test)]` modules of drain.rs, main.rs and display.rs.

decisions.choice: Identify the drain by pid file plus a process start marker (Linux /proc/<pid>/stat field 22 parsed after the last ')', state Z means gone; elsewhere `ps -o lstart=,stat= -p <pid>`).
decisions.reason: A pid can be recycled and `athena_agent::procs::process_alive` (kill -0) cannot tell a recycled pid from the drain. The start time survives exec, so the drain that execs into the rebuilt binary (`follow_restart` -> `reexec`, main.rs:583) keeps a valid file. setup.sh supports Darwin (setup.sh:16-17), so a `ps -p` fallback keeps macOS from a weaker check without matching text.

rejected.why: This is the failure class: it matches the matcher's own command line and any process whose arguments contain the word.
A recycled pid would be reported as the drain.
Needs unsafe libc calls or a new dependency (the workspace denies unsafe_code), and a lock cannot report pid, build and start time.

decisions.choice: `drain-stop` keeps writing `drain.stop`; `--wait [--timeout SECS]` polls the pid file until the drain has exited, with no limit unless `--timeout` is given, printing a progress line every 30 s. No signal is sent.
decisions.reason: Stop semantics (finish the job, stop at a job boundary, main.rs:1234-1243, drain.rs:133) stay. 'No unrelated process is signalled' holds by construction. A single job can run for hours, so a default timeout would only abandon a stop that is still correctly pending.

rejected.option: SIGTERM the pid from the file
rejected.why: Kills mid-job, contradicting 'stop at a job boundary'; needs unsafe or a new dependency; could hit a recycled pid.
One job can outlast it, leaving the stop pending while the caller believes it failed (finding 2).

decisions.choice: `restart` order: (a) rebuild, a failure returns at once touching nothing; (b) read `drain_state`; (c) if Running, `stop_and_wait`; if NotRunning(Missing), print that a drain started by a build without the pid file cannot be seen, write NO stop file, and go on; (d) once the old drain is gone and the first rebuild was `Installed`, call `Lifecycle::installed_stale()`; if it gives a line, rebuild again (nothing lands now, the old drain has exited) and check again; a failed rebuild or a line that remains returns Err naming that no drain is running and the command to run (`./setup.sh`, then `athena drain`); (e) spawn the installed binary with the drain flags (via `reexec_args`, drain.rs:485); (f) poll until the pid file names a live pid other than the old one, then print pid and build; if the new process dies first, fail naming `drain.log` and its last lines.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 1: rebuild_if_due holds `self.landing` for the whole setup.sh run because a landing moves the checkout the build reads (drain.rs:2430-2436). `restart` cannot take that lock in another process, so a landing by the old drain between the first rebuild and its exit can leave the installed binary behind HEAD or built from a half-updated tree. Re-checking after the old drain exits closes that window, since nothing lands once it is gone. The first rebuild still comes first, so a broken build never takes the old drain down. The check must read the INSTALLED binary: `Athena::stale_build` (status.rs:1709) compares `self.build`, which is the running restart process's own old build and would always look stale after a rebuild. `RealLifecycle::installed_stale` runs `<wiring::installed_binary()> --version` (output `athena <version> (commit <sha>[, dirty])`, tests/version.rs:48), parses the commit with a pure function, and calls `athena_core::status::stale_build_line(&athena.git, commit, &athena.head()?)` (status.rs:35, lib.rs:229). `run_setup` and the installed binary are the same build: setup.sh runs xtask `setup` which installs to `paths::athena_home().join("bin/athena")` (xtask/src/main.rs:538) = `installed_binary()` (wiring.rs:63).

rejected.option: Stop the old drain first, then rebuild only
rejected.why: A failed rebuild would leave no drain running; the chosen order keeps the old drain until a rebuild has succeeded at least once.

rejected.option: Let the new drain's `guarded` find the stale build and report that the process died
rejected.why: The queue sits idle (the evidence-1 failure) and the person learns it only from drain.log.
It reads the running binary's build, not the installed one, so it is wrong in `restart`.

rejected.option: Take the drain's landing lock from `restart`
rejected.why: The lock is an in-process Mutex; another process cannot hold it.

decisions.choice: `drain-restart` and `drain-stop --wait` take `--timeout`; without it they wait without limit. On timeout `restart` returns an error saying: the stop is still asked for, no new drain was started, the old drain (pid N) will exit at its next job boundary, then run `athena drain-restart` again or `athena drain`. Exit code 2.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 2: a timeout must not leave an idle queue unexplained.

rejected.option: Remove the stop file on timeout
rejected.why: Would silently cancel a stop the person asked for.

decisions.choice: `guarded(state_root, procs, build, stale, run)`: call `stale()`; refuse with 'refusing to start the drain: <line>; nothing was dispatched'; else `PidGuard::acquire`, which reports whether the previous record was this very pid (exec carry-over); remove `drain.stop` only when it was not (file missing, dead or recycled); then run.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 4: after an in-drain rebuild the exec'd binary has the same pid (drain.rs:3021 checks `stop_requested` before `restart` is set, then `reexec`), so a stop written in that window belongs to this run and must survive. Acquiring before clearing means a refused second start does not delete the first drain's pending stop. One production entry point, testable in drain.rs with the existing `Stub`.

rejected.why: Loses a stop requested between the last check and the exec.
Needs the Fixture from tests/common, which only integration tests can use, forcing a test file outside the deliverables.
Shared with `Steps` stubs and has no `Athena`.

decisions.choice: `spawn_detached` uses `process_group(0)` (safe `CommandExt`), stdin null, output appended to `<state>/drain.log`. Help and README say the restarted drain runs in the background in its own process group, not its own session, and logs to `<state>/drain.log`.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 5 without unsafe code (the workspace denies it). Claiming a full detach would be wrong.

rejected.why: Not present on every host (macOS); adds a dependency on an external tool for a nit. Left as a possible follow-up.

decisions.choice: Exit codes: `drain-status` 0 running, 2 not running; `drain-stop --wait` and `drain-restart` 2 on timeout; errors 1.
decisions.reason: Matches the convention that 2 means 'did not reach the state' (main.rs:1218); scripts can test without parsing text.

rejected.why: A script cannot tell running from not running.

decisions.choice: All new tests go in the `#[cfg(test)]` modules of drain.rs (from line ~3962; `Kept` UI at drain.rs:4199 captures lines), main.rs (tests at ~1492, which already render `Cli::command()` help) and display.rs (tests at ~1762). tempfile is a dev-dependency.
decisions.reason: Keeps every file inside the reading's six deliverables.

rejected.option: New tests/drain_lifecycle.rs or append to tests/drain.rs

decisions.reason: The change adds no parser, stem list, stop list or reading check over request text. The new refusals are process and build checks. `crates/athena-core/tests/refusal_corpus.rs` has no match for drain, stale or pid (searched in round 1); it still runs in `cargo test --locked`.

rejected.option: Corpus cases for the new refusals
rejected.why: The corpus covers request-form inputs, not process state.

Add the unit tests for criteria 1-6 in the existing tests module. Do not change `follow_restart`, `stop_file`, `rebuild_if_due` or the `Steps` trait.

Add `DrainStatus`, `DrainRestart` and `DrainStop --wait/--timeout` with help text pointing away from pkill/pgrep and stating the background/log behaviour. Run `Command::Drain` inside `drain::guarded`. Add dispatch arms and exit codes. Add the unit tests for criteria 8 and 9.
Add `spawn_detached(binary, args, cwd, log) -> io::Result<u32>` (stdin null, output appended to the log, own process group, no unsafe).

Unreleased/Added entry: root cause (processes found by matching text), `drain-status`, `drain-restart`, `drain-stop --wait`, the pid file, the stale-binary refusal, the 5% figure labelled an estimate, the one-time transition for drains started without a pid file, and that the resume command is a separate item.

Extend 'Stopping a drain' with `--wait`; add a paragraph on the pid file, `drain-status`, `drain-restart` (rebuild, wait, re-check, start in the background, log at `<state>/drain.log`), the stale-build refusal and the one-time transition.

steps: drain.rs: add `pid_file(state_root)` (`drain.pid`), `PidRecord {pid, started, build, at}` (serde JSON), the `Procs` trait and `RealProcs`. Linux: read /proc/<pid>/stat, take the text after the last ')', read the state and starttime, return None if the file is missing or the state is Z. Elsewhere: `ps -o lstart=,stat= -p <pid>`. Each parser is a pure function with unit tests (a command name containing spaces and parentheses; sample `ps` text).

drain.rs: add `DrainState` (`Running(PidRecord)` or `NotRunning(Reason)`, Reason = Missing, Unreadable(why), Dead(pid), Recycled(pid)), `drain_state(state_root, procs)`, `write_record`, and `PidGuard::acquire(state_root, procs, pid, build)` using `create_new`. A live record naming another pid is refused with 'a drain is already running (pid N)'. A stale record, or one naming this pid, is replaced; `acquire` reports whether the previous record named this pid. `Drop` removes the file only if it still names the guard's pid.

drain.rs: add `stop_and_wait(state_root, procs, wait: Option<Duration>, poll, ui)`: always writes `drain.stop` (creating the directory), sends no signal, prints a progress line every 30 s while waiting, and returns Asked, Exited, TimedOut or NotRunning. Add the `Lifecycle` trait (`procs`, `rebuild() -> Result<Rebuild, String>`, `installed_stale() -> Option<String>`, `spawn() -> Spawned {pid, log}`) and `restart(state_root, &dyn Lifecycle, Waiting, ui)` in the order: rebuild (Err returns at once, touching nothing); `drain_state`; if Running, `stop_and_wait` (a TimedOut returns Err saying the stop is still asked for, no new drain was started, the old pid and what to run next); if Missing, print the older-build notice and write no stop file; once the old drain is gone and the first rebuild was `Installed`, call `installed_stale()` and, on a line, rebuild again and check again (Err naming that no drain is running and the command to run if the rebuild fails or the line remains); spawn; poll until the pid file names a live pid other than the old one; if the spawned pid dies first, Err with the log path and its last lines. Return a `RestartReport` with old pid, new pid and build.

drain.rs: add `RealLifecycle` (rebuild = `run_setup(athena.git.dir())`; `installed_stale` = run `wiring::installed_binary() --version`, parse the commit with the pure `commit_in_version`, then `athena_core::status::stale_build_line(&athena.git, commit, &athena.head()?)`, None when anything cannot be read; spawn = `wiring::spawn_detached` with `reexec_args(..)`). Add `guarded(state_root, procs, build: &str, stale: &dyn Fn() -> Option<String>, run)`: call `stale()` first and return Err('refusing to start the drain: <line>; nothing was dispatched'); then `PidGuard::acquire`; remove `drain.stop` only when the previous record did not name this pid; then call `run`.

wiring.rs: add `spawn_detached(binary, args, cwd, log) -> io::Result<u32>` (`Command` with stdin null, stdout/stderr appended to the log, `process_group(0)`, no unsafe). main.rs: add `DrainStatus {json}`, `DrainRestart {budget, rating_threshold, job_limit, timeout}` and `DrainStop {wait, timeout}`, with help text saying to use these instead of pkill/pgrep/wait loops, that the pid file is the only thing consulted, and that a restarted drain runs in the background in its own process group and logs to `<state>/drain.log`. Wire `Command::Drain` to run `drain_concurrent` and `follow_restart` inside `drain::guarded`, passing `wiring::version_string(&athena.build)` and `&|| athena.stale_build()`, and drop the `warn_if_stale` call there only. Exit codes: status 0/2, `--wait` and restart timeout 2.

display.rs: add `drain_status(&DrainState, stop_asked: bool)`, `drain_stop(&StopOutcome)` and `drain_restart(&RestartReport)`. Each says in words why a drain counts as not running; restart prints the build started. Add a small test in display.rs's tests module.

drain.rs tests module: write the lifecycle tests named in the demonstrations (criteria 1-6, with 6 sharing criterion 3's test), using `tempfile`, `Stub`, `Kept` and real children from `Command::new("sleep")` / `sh -c`, with `arg0` for the self-naming case. Reap every child, and join the watcher threads.

CHANGELOG.md: add the Unreleased/Added entry (root cause: processes found by matching text; the fix: pid file, three commands, stale refusal, re-check after the old drain exits; the 5% estimate, not measured; the one-time transition for a drain started without a pid file; the resume command is a separate item).

README.md: extend 'Stopping a drain' and add a paragraph on `drain-status`, `drain-restart`, the pid file, the stale-build refusal, the background run and the transition. Then run `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`.

risks.risk: A landing by the old drain between `restart`'s first rebuild and the old drain's exit leaves the installed binary behind HEAD or torn, so the new drain would refuse to start (finding 1).
risks.mitigation: After the old drain has exited, `restart` asks `installed_stale()` (installed binary's commit versus HEAD) and rebuilds again with nothing landing; a failed or still-stale result spawns nothing and tells the person no drain is running and to run ./setup.sh. Criterion 4 cases (c) and (d) test it.

risks.risk: The old drain runs a long job, so `restart` waits a long time, and a timeout would leave a pending stop and no new drain (finding 2).
risks.mitigation: No limit by default with a progress line every 30 s; with `--timeout` the error states the stop is still asked for, no new drain started, and what to run next. Tested in case (e).

risks.risk: On the first restart after this ships a running older drain has no pid file, so `restart` cannot see it and starts a second drain beside it (finding 3).
risks.mitigation: `restart` prints the notice, writes no stop file (the new drain would clear it), and the README and CHANGELOG state the one-time transition and tell the person to run `athena drain-stop` and wait for the old drain before the first restart. The job lock (athena-core/src/run/mod.rs:365) still stops one job running twice.

risks.risk: A stop requested between the old image's last stop check and the exec is lost (finding 4).
risks.mitigation: `guarded` keeps `drain.stop` when the record names this pid; tested in criterion 5 case (3).

risks.risk: The restarted drain is in its own process group but the caller's session, so a terminal hangup might still reach it (finding 5).
risks.mitigation: Help and README say plainly it runs in the background in its own process group, logs to `<state>/drain.log`, and that `athena drain-status` shows whether it is alive. `restart` confirms the new pid before reporting success.

risks.risk: After an in-drain rebuild the exec'd binary can refuse to start if its build commit is still behind HEAD, ending a long run with an error.
risks.mitigation: This is the intended protection; the message says to run ./setup.sh or `athena drain-restart`. `stale_build_line` returns None when the build commit is unknown or not an ancestor (status.rs:36-40), so odd builds are not blocked. The guard returns Err and removes the pid file.

risks.risk: A drain killed with SIGKILL leaves a stale `drain.pid`.
risks.mitigation: The start-marker check counts a dead or recycled pid as not running, status says why, and the next `acquire` replaces the file.

risks.risk: Two drains start at the same moment.
risks.mitigation: `acquire` creates the file with `create_new`; if it exists it is inspected, a stale one removed and `create_new` retried once, so only one start wins.

risks.risk: Tests with real child processes are flaky (timing, zombies).
risks.mitigation: Children are reaped explicitly, poll intervals are short, waits have generous timeouts, and the zombie case is handled in code (state Z means gone), not by timing.

risks.risk: The detached spawn loses output or its working directory.
risks.mitigation: `spawn_detached` runs in the repository root and appends output to `<state>/drain.log`; if the pid file does not show the new pid in time, `restart` fails and prints the log path and its last lines.

risks.risk: The non-Linux `ps -p` marker cannot be run in this environment's tests.
risks.mitigation: Its parser is a pure function tested on sample `ps` text; the criterion 8 scan requires `-p` on every `ps` call; the CHANGELOG states which platforms were tested.

risks.risk: `guarded` takes the stale check as a closure, so a wiring mistake in main.rs would not be caught by the unit test.
risks.mitigation: The wiring is one line, `&|| athena.stale_build()`, required by plan step 5; the detection is covered by the existing tests/drain.rs test.

demonstrations.method: Unit test in drain.rs's tests module over the production `drain_state`, `display::drain_status` and `stop_and_wait`, with real children and a tempdir state root. The 'drain' child is a `sleep` whose argv[0] is `athena drain --budget 5` (safe `CommandExt::arg0`). A decoy `sleep` also has `athena drain` in its argv and no pid file. The test writes `drain.pid` for the drain child through the production `write_record` with the marker from `RealProcs.start_marker(child.id())`.
demonstrations.observes: `drain_state` returns Running with the drain child's pid and never the decoy. The printed status holds that pid, the build and 'running'. `stop_and_wait` with no wait returns Asked and creates `drain.stop`. With a wait and a child that exits once the stop file appears, it returns Exited. The decoy is still alive at the end. No code path reads command text.
demonstrations.fails_without: A text-matching implementation reports the decoy (or none) as running. With no pid-file lookup, status says 'not running' for the live child and the Running assertion fails. With no wait, the Exited assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: Entry points `drain::drain_state`, `drain::stop_and_wait`, `display::drain_status`. The injection point is the `Procs` trait; the test passes `&RealProcs` over real child processes, so there is no fake. `Procs`, `RealProcs`, `write_record`, `drain_state`, `stop_and_wait` are added in plan steps 1-3, `display::drain_status` in step 6. `drain::stop_file` (drain.rs:970) exists.

demonstrations.method: Unit test of `drain_state` and `stop_and_wait` over: no file; unreadable JSON; a file naming a child killed and reaped (true marker saved while alive); a file naming a killed but unreaped child (zombie); a file naming a live unrelated `sleep` child with a wrong marker (recycled pid).
demonstrations.observes: Each case returns NotRunning with its own reason (missing, unreadable, dead, recycled). The status printer says 'no drain is running' and the exit-code mapping function returns 2. `stop_and_wait` returns NotRunning and still writes `drain.stop`. The recycled-pid child is still alive afterward (`try_wait()` is None), so nothing signalled it.
demonstrations.fails_without: A pid-only check (`process_alive`) reports the recycled and zombie cases as running. With no unreadable-file guard, the garbage file is treated as running or panics.
demonstrations.seam: `drain::drain_state`, `drain::stop_and_wait`, `RealProcs`, real children, tempdir state root. Added in plan steps 1-3; no fake.

demonstrations.method: Unit test calling the production `drain::guarded(state_root, &RealProcs, build, &stale, || drain::drain(&stub, limits, &Kept::default()))`. `stale` is a closure returning `Some("stale build: this athena was built from aaaaaaaaaaaa, and 3 file(s) under crates/ ... changed by bbbbbbbbbbbb; run ./setup.sh")`. `stub` is the existing `Stub` steps in drain.rs's tests module (drain.rs:3968), which logs every call. A control case passes a closure returning None.
demonstrations.observes: With the stale closure `guarded` returns Err containing 'refusing to start' and the stale line (both commit ids and 'crates/'). The `Stub` call log is empty (no read, run or land), `drain.pid` does not exist, and a pre-existing `drain.stop` is untouched. In the control case the closure runs, the log is non-empty and the pid file is gone afterward. The stale-build detection itself (`stale_build_line`) is unchanged and covered by tests/drain.rs `status_prints_the_stale_build_line_after_a_crates_change_and_none_after_docs_or_records_changes` (line 1993).
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the refusal in `guarded`, the closure runs, the Stub log is non-empty and the result is Ok, so the Err and empty-log assertions fail.
demonstrations.seam: `drain::guarded` is added in plan step 4; the stale answer is injected as a closure parameter, and only the yes/no answer is canned, the refusal logic is in `guarded`. `Stub`, `Kept` and `drain::drain` exist (drain.rs:3968, 4201, 2797). main.rs passes `&|| athena.stale_build()` in step 5.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests calling the production `drain::restart(state_root, &life, waiting, &Kept)` with a `Lifecycle` double `Rec`. `Rec.rebuild` appends 'rebuild' to a shared log and returns a scripted Ok/Err. `Rec.spawn` appends 'spawn', starts a real `sleep` child and writes its pid file through the production `write_record` with build 'athena 0.0.0 (commit abcdef123456)'. `Rec.installed_stale` returns Some(line) while a fake HEAD flag is ahead of the count of successful rebuilds. The old drain is a real `sh -c 'while [ ! -e <stop file> ]; do sleep 0.05; done'` child with a pid file, so it exits only when `restart` creates the stop file; a watcher thread reaps it, logs 'old exited', and (in the race case) advances the fake HEAD, standing in for a landing. Cases: (a) happy path; (b) failed first rebuild; (c) the old drain advances HEAD while restart waits; (d) the second rebuild fails; (e) the old drain never exits and `--timeout` is short; (f) no pid file; (g) the spawned child exits at once.
demonstrations.observes: (a) log is exactly rebuild, old exited, spawn; the report names old pid, new pid and build and `display::drain_restart` prints the build. (b) rebuild Err: restart returns Err carrying the build output, the log is only 'rebuild', no stop file, the old child is alive, no spawn. (c) log is rebuild, old exited, rebuild, spawn: a second rebuild runs before spawn. (d) log is rebuild, old exited, rebuild with no spawn, and the Err says no drain is running and to run ./setup.sh. (e) Err says the stop is still asked for, no new drain was started, and to run `athena drain-restart` again; `drain.stop` still exists; log has no second rebuild and no spawn. (f) the Kept lines contain the notice about drains from builds without a pid file, no `drain.stop` is written, and spawn is logged. (g) Err names `drain.log`. Also a pure-function test of `commit_in_version` on `athena 0.1.0 (commit abc123def456)` and `(commit unknown, dirty)`.
demonstrations.fails_without: If restart spawned before the old drain exited, 'spawn' would precede 'old exited'. If it skipped the rebuild, 'rebuild' would be missing. If a failed rebuild did not abort, 'spawn' would appear or the stop file would exist. Without the post-exit freshness check, case (c) has no second 'rebuild'. Without the timeout message, (e) fails its text assertions.
demonstrations.seam: `drain::restart` and the `Lifecycle` trait are added in plan step 3 (`installed_stale` included). The double supplies only the rebuild result, the stale answer, and the process standing in for the new binary, and it uses the production pid-file writer. Ordering, waiting, the re-check, the timeout and verification are all in `restart`. `RealLifecycle` (which calls `run_setup` at drain.rs:3317, runs the installed `--version` and `wiring::spawn_detached`) is not used in this test; `spawn_detached` is added in step 5. `Kept` exists (drain.rs:4201).

demonstrations.method: Unit test of `PidGuard::acquire` and `drain::guarded` with a tempdir state root. Cases: (1) read `drain.pid` inside the closure; (2) a second `guarded` while a pid file names a live `sleep` child (real pid and marker), with a `drain.stop` present; (3) a file naming the test's own pid and marker (exec carry-over) with a `drain.stop` present; (4) a closure that panics under `catch_unwind`; (5) a leftover file naming a dead pid, with a `drain.stop` present; (6) no file, with a `drain.stop` present.
demonstrations.observes: (1) During the closure the file exists with the test's pid and the build string; after `guarded` returns it is gone. (2) Err 'a drain is already running (pid N)', the closure did not run, the first drain's `drain.stop` still exists. (3) accepted, and `drain.stop` still exists inside the closure (the carried-over stop is kept). (4) the file is gone after the panic. (5) the leftover is replaced and `drain.stop` is removed. (6) `drain.stop` is removed.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the write, the in-closure read fails. Without the Drop removal, the after-exit check fails. Without the live check, the second start runs its closure. If `guarded` always removed the stop file, case (3) or (2) fails.
demonstrations.seam: `drain::guarded`, `PidGuard::acquire` and `Drop` are added in plan steps 2 and 4. `RealProcs` with real children is injected as `&dyn Procs`.

demonstrations.method: The same unit test as criterion 3. Its control half injects a closure that returns None, as a docs-only or records-only change after the build gives (`stale_build_line`, status.rs:35-58, returns None unless BUILD_PATHS changed), and shows the guard runs the closure. The 5% figure is an estimate carried over from the reading and is not measured; the CHANGELOG entry says so.
demonstrations.observes: A start with a stale answer is refused and a start with none is not, so the new refusals are limited to genuinely stale builds. The test does not show the 5% rate.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the guard refused every start or ignored the closure's answer, the control assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: Same as criterion 3: `drain::guarded` (plan step 4) with the stale closure injected.

demonstrations.method: Run the workspace lint with warnings denied, then the format check. The workspace denies `unsafe_code` (athena-cli Cargo.toml:34-35), so new code uses only safe APIs (`CommandExt::process_group` and `arg0`, /proc reads, `ps` by pid, `<installed> --version`).
demonstrations.observes: Exit 0 with no warnings. The verifier then runs `cargo fmt --all --check`, which prints no diff and exits 0.
demonstrations.fails_without: A new `unsafe` block, an unused helper (a `Procs` or `Lifecycle` method or `pid_file` with no caller), a needless clone, or unformatted code makes the command exit non-zero.
demonstrations.seam: The whole workspace compiled under the workspace `[lints]` configuration; no fake or fixture. The seam exists today; the code from plan steps 1-6 and its tests are what is compiled.

demonstrations.method: Unit test in main.rs's tests module (`Cli::command().render_help()` is used at main.rs:1685). It renders help for the top level and for `drain-status`, `drain-restart` and `drain-stop`. A second assertion takes `include_str!` of `drain.rs`, `main.rs` and `wiring.rs`, keeps the text before `#[cfg(test)]`, and asserts none contains `Command::new("pgrep")`, `Command::new("pkill")`, `Command::new("pidof")` or a `/cmdline` read. The needles are built with `format!` so the test file does not contain them. It also asserts that every `Command::new("ps")` argument list contains `-p`.
demonstrations.observes: The top-level help lists `drain-status` and `drain-restart`. Each command's help tells the person to use it instead of pkill or pgrep; `drain-stop --help` mentions `--wait`; `drain-restart --help` says the new drain runs in the background and logs to drain.log. No command-text matching appears in the three files.
demonstrations.fails_without: With the subcommands missing or their help lacking the pkill/pgrep wording, the help assertions fail. If a pgrep, pkill, pidof or /cmdline read were added, the scan fails.
demonstrations.seam: `Cli::command()` in main.rs (used at main.rs:504). The clap variants are added in plan step 5. The scan reads source text with `include_str!`; nothing is injected.

demonstrations.method: Unit test in main.rs's tests module, which already uses `include_str!("../../../athena.toml")` (main.rs:1716), so repository-relative includes work. It reads `CHANGELOG.md` and `README.md`, cuts the CHANGELOG at its first released-version heading to get the Unreleased section, and checks both texts.
demonstrations.observes: The Unreleased section names `drain-status`, `drain-restart`, `drain-stop --wait`, the pid file, the stale-binary refusal and the one-time transition for a drain started without a pid file, and labels the 5% figure an estimate. The README 'Stopping a drain' section mentions `--wait`, `drain-status` and `drain-restart`, and a README paragraph states how the pid file, the stale-build refusal, the background run (`drain.log`) and the transition work.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the CHANGELOG entry or README text were missing or omitted a command name, the substring assertions fail.
demonstrations.seam: `include_str!` of `CHANGELOG.md` and `README.md` from the main.rs tests module. No injection. The text is written in plan steps 9-10.

open_questions: User: `drain-restart` takes the same flags as `drain` (budget required, defaults for the rest) because a stopped drain does not record its remaining limits. Is that acceptable, or should the drain record its limits in the pid file so a restart can reuse them?
